test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 30 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Select the correct chronological order of Acts and policies according to their first appearance in the Indian Constitution and legislative.

options.text: Right to Information Act, Right to Education Act, Right to Person with Disabilities Act, Information Technology Act
Right to Education Act, Information Technology Act, Right of Persons with Disabilities Act, Right to Information Act
Information Technology Act, Right to Information Act, Right to Person with Disabilities Act, Right to Education Act
Information Technology Act, Right to Information Act, Right to Education Act, Right to Person with Disabilities Act

solution:
The correct answer is__** Information Technology Act, Right to Information Act, Right to Education Act, Right to Person with Disabilities Act**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct order is:
 
 
• **Information Technology Act** - 2000
 
• **Right to Information Act** - 2005
 
• **Right to Education Act** - 2009
 
• **Right of Persons with Disabilities Act** - 2016
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Information Technology Act (2000)**:

 
 
• The **Information Technology Act, 2000** was one of the earliest significant legislations focusing on e-commerce, cyber laws, and the regulation of electronic transactions in India.
 
• It was enacted to provide legal recognition to electronic transactions and digital signatures.
 
• This Act forms the foundation for the legal framework surrounding the digital space in India.
 
 
 
• **Right to Information Act (2005)**:
 
 
• The **Right to Information Act, 2005** was introduced to ensure transparency and accountability in the functioning of government institutions.
 
• It empowers citizens to request information from public authorities and holds them accountable for their actions and decisions.
 
• This Act revolutionized citizen participation in governance.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education Act (2009)**:
 
 
• The **Right to Education Act, 2009** came into force to provide free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14 years.
 
• It guarantees the right of children to receive elementary education of a certain standard and promotes the involvement of children in schools.
 
• This Act was significant in promoting universal access to education.
 
 
 
• **Right of Persons with Disabilities Act (2016)**:
 
 
• The **Right of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016** was enacted to ensure equal rights and opportunities for persons with disabilities in various spheres such as education, employment, healthcare, and social participation.
 
• It replaced the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995, and broadened the scope of rights for differently-abled individuals.
